issue_context.title: Environment Canada hourly forecast times are incorrect
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The hourly forecast provided by the Environment Canada integration shows times offset by +6h.

My dashboard shows this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/537025/121830665-bcc87280-cc82-11eb-8e0e-25b9aa4caddf.png)

The hourly forecast on the Environment Canada web site (https://weather.gc.ca/forecast/hourly/ab-50_metric_e.html) shows this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/537025/121830723-e5506c80-cc82-11eb-88fb-bf3d0faa55cb.png)

The times shown in the weather card are six hours ahead of the times reported by Environment Canada.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.6.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Core

### Integration causing the issue

environment_canada

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/environment_canada/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
weather:
  - platform: environment_canada
    forecast: hourly
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
There are no error messages, stack traces, etc.  The integration works and pulls accurate data, it's just offset by +6h.
```


### Additional information

_No response_

This seems like a front end issue. The component uses UTC time for the hourly forecasts, but they’re not being translated to the local time zone of the HA installation when displayed.

When I look in Developer Tools > States and look for my weather.edmonton entity, here's what the YAML for the state looks like:

```

  - datetime: '2021-06-15T10:00:00-06:00'
    temperature: 18
    condition: partlycloudy
    precipitation_probability: 10
  - datetime: '2021-06-15T11:00:00-06:00'
    temperature: 17
    condition: partlycloudy
    precipitation_probability: 10
  - datetime: '2021-06-15T12:00:00-06:00'
    temperature: 17
    condition: partlycloudy
    precipitation_probability: 10
friendly_name: Edmonton
```

The first entry is for `2021-06-14T13:00:00-06:00`, but the current local time is 6:45 (MDT) so I'd expect the first entry to be `2021-06-14T07:00:00-06:00`

The XML from Environment Canada (https://dd.weather.gc.ca/citypage_weather/xml/AB/s0000045_e.xml) shows this for the first entry in the hourly forecast:

```
<hourlyForecast dateTimeUTC="202106141300">
<condition>A few showers. Risk of thunderstorms</condition>
<iconCode format="png">19</iconCode>
<temperature unitType="metric" units="C">17</temperature>
<lop category="High" units="%">100</lop>
<windChill unitType="metric"/>
```

It seems like something is treating the UTC times from Environment Canada as local times.

I did some more playing around and the following change in homeassistant/components/environment_canada/weather.py fixes it for me:

```
--- weather.py.orig     2021-06-14 20:24:50.885435728 -0600
+++ weather.py  2021-06-14 20:22:35.133916041 -0600
@@ -236,7 +236,7 @@
             forecast_array.append(
                 {
                     ATTR_FORECAST_TIME: dt.as_local(
-                        datetime.datetime.strptime(hours[hour]["period"], "%Y%m%d%H%M")
+                        datetime.datetime.strptime(hours[hour]["period"], "%Y%m%d%H%M").replace(tzinfo=dt.UTC)
                     ).isoformat(),
                     ATTR_FORECAST_TEMP: int(hours[hour]["temperature"]),
                     ATTR_FORECAST_CONDITION: icon_code_to_condition(
```

What I think is happening is that the existing strptime call returns a datetime object without a timezone, so all dt.as_local() does is attaches the local timezone to the datetime object.  It doesn't perform any adjustments to the time.  By attaching a timezone using .replace(), the code in dt.as_local() now knows that it is in UTC and can perform the appropriate translations.

After making this change, the frontend shows the correct times and the yaml (Developer Tools > States) shows the correct times and my local timezone.

There is likely a better way to do this.

Thanks, that works for me too. I'll see if I can find a tidier way to do this, which might be having the underlying library return `datetime` objects with a time zone instead of strings in the first place.
I've also fixed this in the custom component version: https://github.com/michaeldavie/home-assistant/commit/c61f4498fcae7c849a462fc6aaf313881dfc6a55
